heroText: Calabar is a laid-back riverside city in southeastern Nigeria, best known across Africa as host of the Calabar Carnival, the continent's biggest December street festival. First-time visitors should explore the National Museum inside the old colonial Residency, walk the riverside Marina Resort, and learn the region's history at the Slave History Museum. Margaret Ekpo International Airport connects the city to Lagos and Abuja, and Calabar's clean, walkable streets make it an easy first stop in Nigeria.

areas.name: Marina / Calabar Municipal
areas.text: The Marina district lines the Calabar River in the old town, home to the Marina Resort, National Museum and colonial-era streets, ideal for a first visit on foot.

areas.name: State Housing Estate
areas.text: State Housing Estate is Calabar's modern government and hotel quarter, with wide roads and easy access to restaurants, banks and conference venues.

areas.name: Diamond Hill
areas.text: Diamond Hill is a quiet residential area near the University of Calabar, useful for longer stays close to campus life and local eateries.

areas.name: 8 Miles / Parliamentary Extension
areas.text: The 8 Miles area along Parliamentary Extension holds newer malls, fast-food chains and mid-range hotels, handy for shopping and airport access.

airports.name: Margaret Ekpo International Airport (CBQ)
airports.search: Margaret Ekpo International Airport, Calabar, Nigeria
airports.text: Margaret Ekpo International Airport sits a short drive north of the city centre, with domestic flights to Lagos and Abuja and taxis available outside arrivals.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Margaret Ekpo International Airport (CBQ) and central Calabar before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in the Marina district for an easy first Calabar stay near the museums and riverside resort, or choose State Housing Estate for business trips close to hotels and offices. Diamond Hill suits longer stays near the university, while 8 Miles offers newer malls and quick airport access.
hotelIntro: Calabar hotel choice depends on purpose: the Marina area suits first-time visitors wanting museums and riverside walks within reach, State Housing Estate suits business travelers needing conference hotels, and 8 Miles suits shoppers wanting quick airport access without staying downtown.
rentalCars: A rental car is useful for day trips to Obudu Mountain Resort or Cross River National Park, though taxis and ride-hailing cover the compact city centre fine.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the Marina district for an easy first stay close to museums, the riverside resort and central restaurants without needing a car.

travelTips.title: Carnival season
travelTips.text: Book hotels well ahead for December, when the Calabar Carnival fills the city and rooms sell out across every price range.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Arrange a taxi or hotel pickup at Margaret Ekpo International Airport, since ride-hailing coverage can be patchy for late-night arrivals.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Set aside a full day for Obudu Mountain Resort or Cross River National Park, both a multi-hour drive from the city centre.

nearbyIdeas.name: Obudu Mountain Resort
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Obudu Mountain Resort sits high in the Sankwala hills with cool weather, hiking trails and a cable car, a popular multi-day escape from Calabar.

nearbyIdeas.name: Cross River National Park
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Cross River National Park protects rainforest and rare primates including gorillas, reached by a long drive northeast of the city.

nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Kwa Falls is a forest waterfall a short drive from Calabar, good for a half-day swim and walk through surrounding rainforest.

history.text: In addition to letters and parcels, it also delivered newspapers, and cargo and carried up to 100 passengers to Lagos, Port Harcourt and Calabar.

history.label: 15th century
history.text: Seaport, slave trade When Portuguese explorers in the 15th century reached this part of the Guinea coast, they called the tribes of the area "Calabar".

history.label: 16th century
history.text: Since the 16th century, Calabar has served as an international seaport, exporting such goods as palm oil.
In 1815 HMS Comus, as part of the British blockade of Africa, sailed into Duke Town, where she captured seven Spanish and Portuguese slave ships.

Among the missionaries, Hope Waddell, who worked in Calabar from 1845 to 1858, and Mary Slessor, who evangelized Christianity in Calabar from 1876 to 1915, worked to improve treatment by and among the native.
In 1846, Scottish Presbyterians established a mission station in Calabar.
On 10 September 1884, Queen Victoria signed a treaty of protection with the king and chiefs of Akwa Akpa, known to Europeans as Old Calabar—then the official title to distinguish it from New Calabar.
Calabar was the headquarter of the European administration in the Niger Delta until 1906 when the seat of government was moved to Lagos.
Herbert Macaulay, a newspaper owner and grandson of Samuel Ajayi Crowther, in 1923 founded the first Nigerian political party, the Nigeria National Democratic Party.
In 1926, Governor Graeme Thomson attempted to introduce a poll tax in southeast Nigeria, including Calabar.
It remained the strongest party in the elections until 1939.

Several administrative buildings were destroyed and more than 50 women died at the hands of colonial forces. Biafra War After independence in 1960, tensions increased between the North and South areas of the country.
The Southeastern area decided to become independent and declared itself as the Republic of Biafra in 1967.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: During the centuries of the Atlantic slave trade, it became a major port for shipment of African slaves to the Americas.
